list: Get the complete written cost breakdown upfront: Ask for base annual rent, agency fee, legal fee, refundable caution deposit, and service charge in writing before committing.

Check the prepaid meter and DisCo tariff band: Punch the meter code or inspect the last token receipt to confirm the tariff band (Band A to E) and verify zero inherited arrears.

body: House-hunting in Nigeria teaches you one lesson very quickly: the annual rent written on the advert is only the starting number. body.h2: Understanding Sitting tenant rights on sale in Nigeria

body: When evaluating Sitting tenant rights on sale in Nigeria, start with the legal framework. In Lagos State, the Lagos State Tenancy Law 2011 restricts advance rent demands to one year for new tenants in covered areas (noting that Ikoyi, Victoria Island, Apapa, and Ikeja GRA are exempted from the 2011 statute). list: Get the complete written cost breakdown upfront: Ask for base annual rent, agency fee, legal fee, refundable caution deposit, and service charge in writing before committing.

Visit the property twice (daytime and evening): Check water pressure, wall dampness, and roof ceilings at noon, then check street security, parking, and generator noise after 6:30 p.m.
Film a move-in condition inventory: Record dated video of every tap, socket, tile, door lock, and wall before moving in so your caution deposit refund is indisputable.
Match the recipient bank account name: Only transfer rent to a bank account whose legal name matches the verified landlord or formally mandated corporate manager.

title: First-time renter checklist: 6 Questions to Ask the Agent or Landlord Before Paying
excerpt: Before committing to a rental in Nigeria, use this field checklist on First-time renter checklist to avoid hidden charges, meter debt and agreement disputes.
body: If you have ever stood in an empty flat in Nigeria while an agent tells you "three other people are ready to pay today," you know how artificial pressure works. Slow down and check First-time renter checklist properly first.

body.h2: Understanding First-time renter checklist in Nigeria

body: When evaluating First-time renter checklist in Nigeria, start with the legal framework. In Lagos State, the Lagos State Tenancy Law 2011 restricts advance rent demands to one year for new tenants in covered areas (noting that Ikoyi, Victoria Island, Apapa, and Ikeja GRA are exempted from the 2011 statute). A proposed Lagos Tenancy Bill has also been debated to cap agency fees at 5% of annual rent with a ₦1,000,000 fine for violations, though as of late 2026 that proposal has not yet been enacted into law. Knowing what is current law versus proposed reform helps you negotiate firmly and realistically.

body.h2: Six direct questions to ask about First-time renter checklist

list: Get the complete written cost breakdown upfront: Ask for base annual rent, agency fee, legal fee, refundable caution deposit, and service charge in writing before committing.
Refuse inspection fees for ordinary rental viewings: Legitimate agents earn from completed leases, not from charging visitation fees to open doors.
Check the prepaid meter and DisCo tariff band: Punch the meter code or inspect the last token receipt to confirm the tariff band (Band A to E) and verify zero inherited arrears.
Visit the property twice (daytime and evening): Check water pressure, wall dampness, and roof ceilings at noon, then check street security, parking, and generator noise after 6:30 p.m.
Film a move-in condition inventory: Record dated video of every tap, socket, tile, door lock, and wall before moving in so your caution deposit refund is indisputable.
Match the recipient bank account name: Only transfer rent to a bank account whose legal name matches the verified landlord or formally mandated corporate manager.
